extracted.intended_audience: agency administrators and OMB/policy staff evaluating/applying the OMB circular on employee parking
extracted.subtask_description: Internal agency memoranda commenting on the proposed OMB circular on employee parking, evaluating whether an agency (here, CIA) should be exempt or how to design parking charges and compensating measures. Focuses on operational, equity, security, administrative, and behavioral criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-specific distinctions (location, facilities, public transportation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are clear distinctions that have to be made between agencies concerning location, facilities, public transportation, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the agency in the aggregate only after accounting for its particular location, availability of public transit, and facilities; the memo emphasizes Langley-specific issues (proximity to Beltway, lack of nearby housing) that alter the impact of a parking fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee cover/security considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: One major consideration that may be limited to CIA is the employee cover issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security/cover constraints can limit carpooling or public commuting options (e.g., mixing overt and covert personnel in carpools can compromise cover) and must be weighed when applying generalized parking policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee residential distribution / commuting distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic ratios of where employees reside (e.g., 77% Virginia, 19% Maryland, 2% District, 1% West Virginia) affect commuting patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use employee residence data to assess realistic transit and carpooling options; dispersion implies longer commutes and fewer alternatives to single-occupancy driving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and adequacy of public transportation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is practically no public transportation and what there is available is limited to the District and Virginia; limited bus service to Maryland with attempts to reduce service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If public transit is effectively unavailable, a parking fee will not produce intended modal shifts; assess transit coverage and service levels before imposing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee dispersion and resulting carpooling opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of dispersion, the opportunity for carpooling is reduced considerably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider housing affordability and spatial dispersion that reduce co-located commutes; low co-location reduces feasible carpooling rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of shift workers, handicapped employees, and job-role constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 400 employees work shifts and would be precluded from carpooling; about 100 employees are handicapped and forced to use other public transportation; many supergrade employees may not be able to take advantage of carpooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify subpopulations (shift workers, handicapped, high-clearance roles) that cannot reasonably carpool or use transit when estimating potential behavior change and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing carpooling participation and marginal potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the remaining employees assigned to Headquarters, almost X employees already carpool; any additional increase would be insignificant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure current carpool rates by directorate (noted 34–38% in most directorates, 15% in DCI area) and evaluate marginal gains versus disruption; high existing uptake implies limited additional benefit from fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on employee morale and indirect work contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The loss in 'free' overtime put in by our employees would be severe if parking policy changes reduce their willingness/ability to contribute extra hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess behavioral spillovers such as reduced voluntary overtime or after-hours activities that could hurt mission effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and management costs of implementing paid parking
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional management costs to be incurred to handle a very marginal increase in carpooling certainly does not appear to be cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate staffing, time, and systems costs for fee collection, permit differentiation, monitoring, and enforcement; compare administrative costs to expected benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of fee implementation (timing and compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charge the full fee effective 1 October 1979 rather than phased increases; increase salary of all Federal employees by one half of the average parking fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider one large behavioral-inducing fee versus phased increases, and whether to offset fees with salary adjustments to avoid undue hardship and preserve intent that fees are not revenue devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee structure and incentive effects (drive alone vs carpools)
rubrics_metrics.description: If employee drives alone net cost would be one half the parking fee; two-person carpool no net cost; three-person or larger carpool each participant realizes net savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model different carpool sizes and net costs under proposed compensation changes to predict incentive strength and distributional effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of parking scarcity as justification
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main OMB arguments to subsidized parking in some facilities is that many employees have been forced to public transportation because of limited parking spaces. That is certainly not the case at the CIA Headquarters building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether parking scarcity actually exists; if parking is abundant, scarcity-based justification for subsidies does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity and regressivity / external subsidies to contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears that federal employees would be burdened with a regressive tax while the government would be subsidizing the parking of the private sector at companies under contract who provide free parking to their employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate distributional impacts (regressive burden on employees) and identify indirect government subsidies to private contractors which might create arbitrary distinctions if only federal employees are charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative differentiation and market valuation of parking spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: How would fees be assessed? Surely those parking inside the building would be charged considerably more than those who park in the west parking lot. Since there is no commercial parking available locally and the rental value for the space paid to GSA is less than $10.00 monthly, it would appear that the Agency has every right to receive an exemption in accord with the circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider geographically differentiated pricing, local market rates for parking, and whether low GSA rental values support exemption or special treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offsite spillover and local environmental impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: If paid parking is imposed here at Headquarters, there is a good possibility that employees will park outside the Agency compound in residential areas, along route 123, etc. This situation will obviously be the cause for an environmental impact study by Fairfax County officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential for spillover parking into neighboring residential areas, traffic/environmental impacts, and likely local government responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on after-hours work and employee training
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a number of employees who work late hours, attend educational courses after-hours in the building, etc. A very real problem would arise if they declined to undertake these efforts because transportation is not available for them during late evening hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether parking/ticketing policy will reduce participation in late-shift duties or training programs due to lack of transit options at off-hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the spirit of the circular and current program effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The current carpool program already occupies a large share of the parking space at Headquarters; the Agency is, in fact, already in compliance with the spirit of the OMB circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document existing programs and capacity (carpool programs, preferential parking) and evaluate whether the agency already meets the circular's objectives before imposing new fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and monitoring capacity for carpool permits
rubrics_metrics.description: We have been repeatedly informed that there are not sufficient resources available to monitor closely the misuse of carpool permits. How will the Agency be able to handle the additional carpools which might result from a paid parking scheme?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability to verify/carve out legitimate carpools, monitor misuse, and enforce eligibility; insufficient enforcement undermines policy effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for out-of-pocket costs comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The circular incorrectly implies that there are no 'out-of-pocket' costs for those who drive to work as compared with those who utilize public transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full out-of-pocket cost comparisons (fuel, maintenance, parking fees, time costs) when comparing driving to transit to avoid misleading conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternative measures (e.g., eliminate preferential parking, affirmative action)
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggressive affirmative action program, to include the possible elimination of the preferential parking system, and whatever other innovative ideas that could be developed are a better approach, at least at Langley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate non-fee alternatives (removing preferential parking, affirmative measures, targeted incentives) that may achieve objectives with fewer adverse effects than broad parking charges.
